results.fact: How the Upper Royal Basin camp is booked
results.correct_value: Upper Royal Basin is not bookable on Recreation.gov; it is reserved by calling the Olympic Wilderness Information Center (Royal Lake and the lower zones are booked online).
results.evidence: Two independent backpacking guides state Upper Royal Basin permits are not on Recreation.gov and are obtained through the park's Wilderness Information Center / ranger station by phone. WTA confirms online booking applies to Royal Lake. itinerary.cal, day-1 note, access.permit and the trailhead waypoint already say this; only bivy[0].permit ('same quota permit as Royal Lake... advance reservation only, mid-April release') is wrong, and bivy is owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch. access.overnight_permit.where speaks only of the Royal Lake quota and is not wrong.

results.fact: Direction from Upper Royal Basin camp to Surprise Col
results.correct_value: From Upper Royal Basin the Clark-Johnson col (Surprise Col) lies west-northwest, up Surprise Basin on the basin's west wall.
results.evidence: Published coordinates put Mount Clark at 47.8355,-123.2318 and Mount Johnson (0.26 mi SW of Clark) at 47.8327,-123.2373, so their col is at roughly 47.834,-123.235 — west-northwest of Upper Royal Basin, which lies east of The Needles. A Mount Deception route description has parties climbing the SE side of Surprise Col from the basin, and a Deception-Clark report traverses NORTH from Deception into Surprise Basin, both consistent with the col being NW of the upper basin, not south/southeast. The row's own camp and col pins agree.

results.correct_value: Col to summit about 1.5-2 hours; camp to summit about 3.5-4 hours (the day note mislabelled the camp-to-summit figure as col-to-summit).
results.evidence: One detailed report times upper Royal Basin to Surprise Col at 1.5-2 h and the col to the summit at about 1.5 h, 3.6 h camp-to-summit in all. A second party left upper-basin camp at 6 pm with about 3.5 h of daylight and summited and returned to the col before sunset, so col-to-summit was well under 2 h. The schedule (col 8:00, summit 9:30-10:00) is right; the note's 3.5-4 h is the camp-to-summit figure.

results.fact: Rappel versus downclimbing the summit slot
results.correct_value: The ~60 ft rappel goes down the north side of the summit block — the slot — replacing its downclimb; the rest of the route is then reversed.
results.evidence: A detailed report describes one 60-ft rappel off the summit block that avoided downclimbing the loose ground below it. A route photo captioned 'Summit Block (north side, which is also the rappel)' shows the rappel line is the north-face slot itself. So rappelling and then downclimbing the slot double-counts it; descent_text, descent and the day-2 schedule already say the rappel replaces the downclimb.

patches.replace: Roughly 60 ft rappel down the north side of the summit block in place of downclimbing the slot, then reverse the rest of the route back to the col.

results.fact: Olympic NP entrance fee at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead
results.correct_value: Only a Northwest Forest / America the Beautiful pass to park at the USFS trailhead, plus the wilderness camping permit for overnights.
results.evidence: The park's own Royal Basin page says a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful Pass is required to park at the USFS Upper Dungeness Trailhead and names no entrance fee; WTA and a separate backpacking guide list the same parking pass plus the backcountry camping permit. The trailhead sits in Olympic National Forest with no park entrance station. access.parking_pass, access.fees and access.passRequired already agree; access.notes' 'standard entrance fee' is the outlier.
